trust_decision.summary: Whether a stored PERMISSIONS predicate is allowed to execute a data-modifying statement while it is evaluated with permission enforcement disabled; at the pinned commit the predicate is computed with perms off and nothing rejects the nested write, so the decision is absent both when the clause is stored and when it is evaluated.

landing_point.why: The summary says writes in a PERMISSIONS clause bypass table permissions, so an engineer looks at the table-permission check that runs the stored predicate with new_with_perms(false) and adds a guard there.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fix (and its error text at fix.diff:373) speaks of DEFINE/ALTER, yet only DEFINE handlers call has_direct_write, so a solver can install the same predicate through ALTER TABLE/FIELD/FUNCTION/PARAM/BUCKET/MODULE ... PERMISSIONS - or have it arrive from a v3_1_x catalog decode - and argue that ALTER is a schema-merge path rather than a definition, that the advisory only names DEFINE, and that the runtime guard still blocks the write at execution; likewise the streaming executor's planner-side function/param permission checks are 'a different engine' and are left as they were.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Read-only helper calls and read-only subqueries inside PERMISSIONS must keep working (Expr::read_only() is false for every custom function call, so validating with it rejects `PERMISSIONS WHERE fn::is_owner()` and `WHERE id IN (SELECT ...)`), and the other new_with_perms(false) callers are not permission predicates: DEFINE EVENT bodies/WHEN clauses, materialized-view refresh, DEFINE API action handlers and ON DELETE CASCADE all run with perms disabled and legitimately write.

O6_input_shapes: permission clause kinds: select / create / update / delete (catalog Permissions::has_direct_write)
storage entry points: DEFINE TABLE, FIELD, FUNCTION, PARAM, MODEL, MODULE, BUCKET, CONFIG API and DEFINE API
direct DML in the predicate: CREATE, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE, RELATE, INSERT
DDL in the predicate: DEFINE, REMOVE, REBUILD, ALTER
nesting: prefix/postfix, throw, binary, return, let, block, if/else, foreach, explain, function-call arguments
runtime-only shapes hidden from the static check: write behind a custom-function body, behind a closure, or behind a subquery
execution paths: legacy Expr::compute predicate frames and the streaming executor's legacy-fallback frames

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ALTER TABLE ... PERMISSIONS (and ALTER FIELD ... PERMISSIONS) writes the stored Permissions straight onto the table/field definition; no has_direct_write check, unlike the DEFINE counterpart
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: ALTER is a schema-merge path, not a DEFINE; the advisory and the new error text name DEFINE, and the runtime guard still stops the write when the predicate runs
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same crate, different module tree: expr/statements/alter vs expr/statements/define (and the doc/ landing point)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ALTER FUNCTION / ALTER PARAM / ALTER BUCKET / ALTER MODULE ... PERMISSIONS store a write-bearing Permission::Specific with no read-only rejection (alter/function.rs:63, alter/param.rs:61, alter/bucket.rs:77, alter/module.rs:48)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: non-table resource definitions; a solver reads them as outside 'table permissions' and as ALTER rather than DEFINE
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: expr/statements/alter, four sibling files, none touched by the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Streaming (planner) DEFINE FUNCTION permission check evaluates the predicate without marking the frame as a permission predicate - second implementation of expr/function.rs:285
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the fix converted the legacy compute path only; this is the planner path and it runs with the caller's permissions, so nothing is bypassed there
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another executor subsystem (exec/physical_expr) from the changed expr/function.rs and the doc/ landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Streaming DEFINE PARAM permission check evaluates the predicate with ctx.clone() and no permission-predicate marker - second implementation of expr/param.rs:157
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: param permissions are not table permissions; the check is only reached when permissions are enabled, so the nested write is still permission-checked

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Catalog compatibility decoders rebuild TableDefinition/ApiDefinition Permission::Specific values from stored bytes (v3_0_0 / v3_1_0 / v3_1_1) with no read-only validation, so a database written by an unfixed build carries a side-effecting predicate across the upgrade/reload boundary
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: that is data migration, not user input; existing data is trusted and the runtime guard covers execution
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: catalog/compat module tree, untouched by the fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second mutation route for the stored Permissions (ALTER ... PERMISSIONS) that reuses the DEFINE machinery but skips the new read-only gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix's own error text (fix.diff:373) already says 'DEFINE/ALTER', and the ALTER handlers duplicate every DEFINE field assignment, so a maintainer writing the ALTER arm simply forgot to add the check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planner-side permission evaluator parallel to the legacy one, needing its own predicate-frame flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this repository genuinely runs two executors (legacy Expr::compute and the streaming planner) and already has duplicate function/param permission checks in both

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second HTTP-surface permission evaluator (custom API route or GraphQL resolver) that computes a stored Permission::Specific itself
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix had to patch api/invocation.rs and buc/controller.rs for exactly this reason; a new surface would repeat the pattern

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate the PERMISSIONS clause with the existing Expr::read_only() (or block writes whenever perms are off / switch every new_with_perms(false) to the new constructor), which rejects legitimate `PERMISSIONS WHERE fn::is_owner()` calls and read-only subqueries and breaks DEFINE EVENT bodies, materialized views, API actions and ON DELETE CASCADE that legitimately write with perms disabled.

out_of_scope_notes: Same mechanism, different clause: DEFINE EVENT WHEN/body expressions are evaluated with new_with_perms(false) at surrealdb/core/src/doc/event.rs:52 and :80 and materialized-view conditions at surrealdb/core/src/doc/table.rs:62, so a write there also runs with enforcement disabled - not a PERMISSIONS clause, so outside this advisory.
